feature: Latest ATSC baseline and national reference editions

ATSC.value: HEVC remains in A/341. VVC and optional LCEVC are specified separately in A/345. Current A/342-3 includes Baseline and LC profiles; A/343 includes later caption extensions, safe-area and font-name provisions.

TTA.value: References 2016 A/341, A/342-3 and A/343 candidate editions and A/332 proposed standard. R1 adds animated-image captions. Later ATSC requirements must be compared individually; a legacy reference is not current-edition adoption.

SBTVD.clause: OG scopes; ABNT normative clauses unavailable
SBTVD.value: Independent Brazilian standards are identified. Public OGs describe VVC/LCEVC, MPEG-H and IMSC1/WebVTT topics, but are non-normative. ABNT requirements and options were not read.

difference: Compare current ATSC provisions with the specific Korean legacy-based clauses and the publicly readable Brazilian guidance; do not infer current-edition equivalence from shared codec names.
impact: Edition differences affect bitstream constraints and signaling. This comparison does not certify receiver interoperability.

feature: HEVC formats, scalable coding and HFR constraints

ATSC.value: Progressive HEVC Main 10 / Scalable Main 10, Main tier, Level 5.2; up to 3840×2160, 8/10-bit, 4:2:0 and square pixels. Legacy SD/interlaced HD have separate constraints. Spatial scaling uses two layers and ×1.5/2/3. Level 5.2 HFR requires temporal sub-layering; its duration equation includes +1 for the minus1 fields. SPS VUI/chroma-location constraints also apply.

TTA.value: Selects progressive 720p/1080p/2160p, 16:9, 60-Hz-region rates, Main 10 / Scalable Main 10, Main tier, Level 5.2. §5.3.4 uses the equation d[0]=2*d[1], whereas current A/341 uses (d[0]+1)=2*(d[1]+1). HFR application conditions and general VUI/chroma constraints also require separate comparison.

SBTVD.page: OG printed pp.3–6 and Annex E
SBTVD.value: OG-03 describes single-layer VVC Main 10 / HDR10 / 4:2:0 and LCEVC guidance. It also contains HEVC and AVC annexes without further operational details. This does not establish HEVC prohibition or receiver-wide non-support.
SBTVD.req: ABNT path and option requirements unverified

difference: The Korean HEVC profile shares core tools but is not clause-identical to current A/341. Brazil has a VVC path, which should also be compared with current A/345 rather than only with HEVC.
impact: The HFR equation mismatch needs standards/errata review. Codec selection alone does not prove that any national receiver rejects every other codec.

ATSC.value: SDR, PQ and HLG have specific bitstream constraints; HLG requires SPS transfer_characteristics=18, BT.2100 primaries/matrix, 10-bit narrow-range representation and chroma-location settings. Optional metadata tools have additional conditions.

feature: Current ATSC VVC profiles, formats and HDR

ATSC.value: CMAF profiles cvvc (constrained baseline), cafr (full-range constrained baseline) and cvvm (multilayer). Main 10 / Main tier / Level 6.1; 10-bit progressive video up to 7680×4320. The supported level permits 4K up to 120 fps and 8K up to 60 fps; 8K 100/120 fps is not included. HDR and multilayer capabilities are optional and constrained when used.

TTA.value: The reviewed Korean terrestrial UHD profile selects HEVC. No corresponding national VVC adoption was identified in this reviewed document set; this is not a claim about every future standard or receiver capability.

SBTVD.value: OG-03 describes single-layer VVC Main 10 with HDR10 and 4:2:0. ABNT profile brands, levels, formats and receiver obligations have not been verified.

difference: ATSC and Brazilian guidance share a VVC technology basis. Shared codec naming is not proof of equal profile/level, HDR or carriage constraints.
impact: Current ATSC offers a direct technical comparison axis for Brazilian VVC, while Korea requires a separate HEVC-versus-VVC comparison.

feature: Audio systems, profiles and receiver-support boundaries

ATSC.page: Part 1 printed p.10 / PDF p.15; Part 3 printed pp.7–11 / PDF pp.12–16
ATSC.value: ATSC defines AC-4 and MPEG-H paths selected by signaled codec. MPEG-H permits Baseline or LC Levels 1–3, with current stream/loudness/DRC/emergency constraints. These transmission specifications do not alone establish dual-codec support in every US receiver.

TTA.value: Selects MPEG-H LC Levels 1–3, 48 kHz, 16/20/24-bit input signals and at most 16 core channels. §6.3 requires receiver decoding capability for LC Levels 1, 2 and 3 within this national profile. AC-4 is not the selected terrestrial UHD coding system.

SBTVD.value: MPEG-H is described in public guidance. Stereo/5.1/immersive configurations are audio channel layouts and bitrate examples, not evidence of LC-only versus Baseline profile requirements.

difference: Korea selects MPEG-H LC; current ATSC defines multiple audio systems and MPEG-H profiles. Shared MPEG-H does not make current MHAS/RAP/DRC constraints identical.
impact: Korean LC decoding requirements are source-backed. Brazilian LC-only support and universal US dual-codec implementation are not established by the cited documents.

feature: MPEG-H MHAS, random access and loudness/DRC deltas

ATSC.value: CRC packet types are prohibited; SYNC/SYNCGAP may be ignored. RAP includes AUDIOSCENEINFO only when ASI is present, with fragment/sample rules. Current text adds descriptor/marker and bitrate/downmix/profile-compatibility constraints. DRC metadata is required, with specified loudness coverage; audio emergency information has a separate clause.

TTA.value: CRC prohibition and mhm1/mhm2 carriage are common. SYNC/SYNCGAP must be ignored; the RAP packet list includes AUDIOSCENEINFO without the current ATSC presence condition. DRC metadata is described conditionally when included. Current ATSC bitrate, compatibility, fragment and emergency details are not all reproduced here.

SBTVD.value: Operational MPEG-H guidance is available, but no complete ABNT MHAS/RAP/DRC clause comparison has been performed.

difference: There are explicit shall-versus-may and RAP-condition differences; matching codec/sample-entry names do not establish identical stream behavior.
impact: Use separate acceptance checks for SYNC handling, RAP/fragment layout, loudness/DRC and emergency metadata.

TTA.text: SYNC handling, RAP conditions and current metadata constraints differ

feature: Caption sample/segment size, timing and decoder expectations

ATSC.value: Broadband DASH segment size is <500K bytes; typical broadcast IMSC1 duration is 1–3 seconds. Live text should specify a maximum duration up to 16 seconds. Safe-area/font-name constraints and expected scrolling/profile support are specified separately.

TTA.value: Broadband ISOBMFF caption sample size is ≤500K bytes; typical IMSC1 duration is 0.5–3 seconds. Live caption data must specify a maximum duration up to 16 seconds. The sample-versus-segment unit, boundary inequality and shall/should differ; current ATSC decoder expectations are not fully mapped by §7.4 signaling.

SBTVD.value: Public guidance identifies technologies but supplies no complete packaging/timing equivalence check.

difference: Related packaging concepts are not equal requirements: the unit, exact size bound, typical duration and obligation level differ.
impact: Check memory limits and live-caption persistence against each national stream specification; no device validation is implied.

TTA.text: Sample/segment unit, size boundary, timing and requirement level differ
